description: TABULA (2009 to 2012) and its follow-up EPISCOPE, both Intelligent Energy Europe projects, developed national residential building typologies on a common concept, first for 13 countries, with country pages now listing about 20, including Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Serbia, Spain, Sweden and Slovenia. Each typology classifies existing homes by size, age and other parameters and gives example buildings with typical construction elements and U-values, heating systems and their performance, typical energy use by carrier, and savings from refurbishment at two quality levels, published in national brochures with building display sheets. The TABULA WebTool calculates the example buildings from all countries online, and EPISCOPE added building stock monitoring, scenario case studies and guidance on non-residential and new buildings. Coverage: residential stocks of participating European countries. Access: free web tool and downloads. Licence: project terms. Caveats: the projects ended years ago, and the example buildings are illustrative types, not statistical samples. Simulation uses are residential archetypes and refurbishment packages for building stock energy models. Related records: the Hotmaps building stock data and the EU Building Stock Observatory.
